sentences.text: This animal belongs to the genus Tarsistes, which contains only one known species called Tarsistes philippii. It is a member of the guitarfish family Rhinobatidae and falls within the class Chondrichthyes.
The creature possessed a long, thin, flat snout that was rounded at the tip.

The underside of the head was covered with small star-shaped prickles except at the base. The head was also covered with larger spinules, including six even larger ones that formed a curve around the eye.
The species is known only from a single dried head found in the Juan Fernández Islands off Chile.

The original specimen was initially assigned to the genus Rhynchobatis by Philippi in 1858 without a specific species name. David Starr Jordan created the new name Tarsistes philippii in 1919 because the genus Rhynchobatis was already taken.
Some researchers suggest that Tarsistes might be a synonym of the genus Pseudobatos.
